Get started with Tempest

Source: vignettes/tempest.Rmd
tempest.Rmd

Tempest brings multi-perspective research workflows to R. Given a question, it assembles a panel of specialist perspectives, searches sources, extracts and verifies claims against exact quotes, and writes a cited report. When you want your findings to carry into future runs or conversations, Tempest pairs with graft so only human-reviewed research enters project memory.

Want to see the whole loop without API keys? Run tempest::tempest_app(demo = TRUE) to try real deputy, dsprrr, shinymcp, and graft execution locally against synthetic evidence.

Pick a workflow

Choose the entry point that matches how you want to work:

Goal Entry point What you get
Generate a cited report from a script tempest_run() Committed Markdown report, sources, claims, and claim-by-span support
Add reproducible R analyses & visuals tempest_researcher() or tempest_researcher_app() Portable HTML article, executed R outputs, saved library, and Graft review
Explore a question interactively tempest_app() or tempest_session() Live multi-expert Co-STORM chat, mind map, evidence tables, and report
Share a completed run with an MCP client tempest_mcp_app() Read-only interactive research card for shinymcp

Install and configure

Install the development package from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("JamesHWade/tempest")

Load Tempest and configure your models and search provider with tempest_config():

library(tempest)

cfg <- tempest_config(
  models = "openai/gpt-5.6-luna",
  search_provider = "wikipedia",
  max_search_results = 4,
  max_sources = 12,
  citation_policy = "claim_verified"
)

Tempest uses ellmer for all model calls. Keep credentials in environment variables (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY)—never in R scripts or saved configs. To set a personal default across sessions, add options(tempest.chat = "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514") (or a configured ellmer Chat object) to .Rprofile.

A few useful configuration levers:

  • models: pass one provider/model string for every role, or a named list for coordinator, expert, writer, mindmap, and judge.
  • search_provider: defaults to "native" (OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google built-in web search, falling back to Wikipedia). Built-in alternatives include "wikipedia", "duckduckgo", "tavily", "brave", "serper", "you", "bing", "searxng", "google", and "azure_ai_search".
  • embed_fn / ragnar_store: attach a ragnar store or embedding function (such as ragnar::embed_openai()) for semantic retrieval over fetched sources or your own document corpus.
  • citation_policy: "source_attributed" turns inline IDs into footnotes; "claim_verified" restricts rendered references to threshold-verified support; "strict" blocks publication if unsupported assertions remain.

Run your first STORM report

tempest_run() executes five stages: discover perspectives, research questions per perspective, draft and refine an outline, write cited sections, and verify and publish the final Markdown report.

Start with two experts, a small question budget, and an output_dir so each completed stage is saved to disk:

result <- tempest_run(
  "What are the main technical and policy barriers to recycling grid-scale batteries?",
  config = cfg,
  n_experts = 2,
  max_questions_per_perspective = 2,
  output_dir = "tempest-runs",
  run_id = "grid-battery-recycling",
  verbose = TRUE
)

If a run is interrupted, call tempest_run() again with the same output_dir, run_id, and resume = TRUE to pick up from the first incomplete stage. Pass parallel_writing = TRUE (with mirai installed) to write grounded sections concurrently.

Inspect the report and evidence

Read the committed report and inspect the exact evidence behind every claim:

cat(tempest_report(result))

sources <- tempest_sources(result)
claims <- tempest_claims(result)
supports <- tempest_claim_supports(result)

head(sources[c("id", "title", "url")])
head(claims[c("claim_id", "claim_text", "verification_status", "support_score")])
head(supports[c("claim_id", "source_id", "quote", "verification_status", "support_score")])

tempest_claim_supports() exposes the exact claim-by-evidence-span judgments— showing which verbatim quote supports, partially supports, or contradicts each claim.

Supply your own expert panel

By default, Tempest generates topic-specific experts. When you know the exact lenses you want, construct profiles with tempest_expert() and pass them to either tempest_run() or tempest_session():

experts <- list(
  tempest_expert(
    name = "Recycling Engineer",
    title = "Battery recovery specialist",
    description = "Focuses on process yield, safety, and industrial scale-up.",
    instructions = "Separate demonstrated plant performance from lab projections.",
    focus_areas = c("hydrometallurgy", "process safety"),
    initial_questions = "Which recovery steps constrain full-scale yield?"
  ),
  tempest_expert(
    name = "Policy Analyst",
    title = "Circular-economy policy specialist",
    description = "Focuses on incentives, standards, and compliance.",
    instructions = "Compare jurisdictions and highlight open regulatory gaps.",
    focus_areas = c("producer responsibility", "recycling standards"),
    initial_questions = "Which policies have measurably raised recovery rates?"
  )
)

result <- tempest_run(
  "Technical and policy barriers to recycling grid-scale batteries",
  config = cfg,
  experts = experts
)

Explore interactively with Co-STORM

When the right questions only emerge through dialogue, use Co-STORM in the console or launch the bundled Shiny workspace:

session <- tempest_session(
  "Grid-scale battery recycling",
  config = cfg,
  n_experts = 3
)

session$warmup(verbose = TRUE)
reply <- session$step(
  "Which bottlenecks are most likely to constrain deployment this decade?"
)
cat(reply$answer)

# Add or retire experts as the discussion evolves
session$add_expert("supply-chain economics")

# Publish and read the committed report
session$publish(style = "executive", include_references = TRUE)
cat(tempest_report(session))

# Save and resume later
tempest_session_save(session, "tempest-runs/grid-battery-session", overwrite = TRUE)
restored <- tempest_session_resume("tempest-runs/grid-battery-session", config = cfg)

For a full browser workspace—chat, mind map, sources, extracted facts, transcript, run review, and optional Graft memory—launch tempest_app():

tempest_app(graft_store = "research-memory")

Or launch the dedicated Researcher app when you want starter briefs, custom R tools, MCP servers, reproducible R analyses, and a browsable saved-report library:

tempest_researcher_app(
  output_dir = "research-reports",
  report_library = TRUE,
  graft_store = "research-memory"
)
